title: Void Ending in a Conjunction with Mercury
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The conjunction is the closest bond the Moon makes: at it, her strength takes on the nature of the planet she has joined, and the doctrine of the fifth quality treats her meeting with the Sun as the strongest of all her figures. A course that closes on a conjunction ends in union rather than separation, the Moon's virtue soaked through with the planet's own nature.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a conjunction with Mercury, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his quicksilver turn of mind. Mercury is intellect's planet: learning, dialectic, geometry, astronomy, writing, and the reading of tongues, with every craft found by subtle talent under his governance. He rules the tongue, the brain, and the sensory memory, and quicksilver among the metals. The electional doctrine guards him closely: a work founded on Mercury must not find him retrograde, burning in the Sun's beams, or under an unfortunate planet's gaze.
